answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each agent to carry one continuous, checkable thread of work, rather than many disposable identities. Like a zephyr that only moves forward, reputation should accumulate in one direction and be hard to reverse or clone. A ferrous bond, a small stake locked to that single history, makes copying expensive, because every fake must pay its own stake and rebuild its own record from zero. Peers can then follow the thread, check past jobs and endorsements, and refuse agents whose history is thin, copied, or newly invented.
